description:
client.rs:614-646 — pub fn extract_response<T>

The doc-comment (client.rs:600-609) states the precedence rule for the call_id collision case:
  1. Errors win (any matching invocation that's an "error" returns MethodError)
  2. First non-error match is deserialized into T

This is the documented "Foo/copy + implicit Foo/set both stamped with the same call_id per RFC 8620 §5.8" case. The contract is sound for that scenario.

But the contract is silent about:

- **What if T is wrong but parseable?** A caller calling extract_response::<EmailGetResponse>(&resp, "r1") when resp.method_responses["r1"][0] is actually a Mailbox/get response will get back a deserialized EmailGetResponse with default-shaped fields (serde_json::from_value will succeed on the structural overlap of any two RFC 8620 method responses since both have accountId and ids/list fields). There is no method-name verification. A caller cannot tell from the error type which method they actually got.

- **The first non-error wins, even when a SECOND non-error match has more data.** RFC 8620 §5.8 says the implicit Foo/set in onSuccessDestroyOriginal carries the destruction confirmation — for the *caller* requesting Foo/copy, the Foo/copy invocation is the primary response. But if the server returns them in the OTHER order (Foo/set first, Foo/copy second, both with the same call_id), extract_response silently returns the Foo/set typed as the caller's expected T. The doc-comment's "the first is the primary response and is what the caller wants" assumes the server's ordering matches the caller's mental model. It is not enforced.

Recommendation: add an optional method_name filter (extract_response_for_method) that verifies the matching invocation's method-name field. The existing extract_response can stay for backward compat. Or document explicitly that the function trusts the call_id alone and that callers needing method-name verification should iterate resp.method_responses themselves.
title: extract_response<T> returns first-match silently when multiple non-error invocations share call_id
